problem: Existing zero-shot VLN methods work only in discrete environments, while zero-shot VLN-CE methods still rely on self-supervised training in simulators (e.g. A2Nav), so a sim-to-real gap remains and there is no truly training-free VLN-CE framework.
motivation: Real-world deployment needs continuous low-level control without simulator-specific training. VLN instructions contain explicit spatial semantics (direction, distance, object relations) that can be expressed as geometric constraints and solved directly instead of learned.
key_idea: Decompose the instruction with an LLM into a DAG of waypoint and object nodes, map its edges to six geometric constraint types from a library, and solve waypoint positions by nonlinear constrained optimization, with a navigation tree and backtracking for multiple or zero solutions.
insight: Explicit geometric constraints turn spatial language into solvable optimization, so no navigation training is needed. Ablations show the constraints and search structure matter: replacing the solver with random sampling drops R2R-CE SR from 33.6 to 7.0, removing backtracking drops it to 21.3, and relaxing constraints drops it to 21.5. Failures are mostly from perception (object not found) and LLM decomposition errors.
method: Instruction decomposition: DeepSeek-R1 splits the instruction into stages, each with one displacement and a direction in {front, right, left, back, unknown}, and object nodes with relation to the path, forming a DAG G.

Constraint library: six constraint types (unary and multi-node, 3-4 nodes) with angle sub-constraint c^a and distance sub-constraint c^d; defaults are Δφ=45°, d=1.5m, Δd=1.5m when unspecified. Edges query the library to build the graph constraint K.

Constraint solver: for each waypoint, maximizes the sum of sub-constraints (P1) subject to min(c)≥0 and a minimum distance L from previous solutions, to produce multiple candidates. Object nodes are filtered by constraint only, using Grounded-SAM-2 detections from RGB-D projected onto a BEV map.
Topological sort: fixes the solving order (parents before children, objects before waypoints under the same parent, objects in instruction order).

Navigation tree: the number of solutions at each level becomes branches; if a level has no feasible solution, the robot backtracks to the nearest unexplored sibling. Navigation ends at the last level.
Local policy: Fast Marching Method moves to the chosen waypoint.

setting.backbone: DeepSeek-R1 (frozen, instruction decomposition) + Grounded-SAM-2 (frozen, perception) + Fast Marching local planner
setting.action_space: waypoints solved by constraint optimization, executed by Fast Marching Method as low-level continuous actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE) plus a real robot

numbers.evidence: Table 1: Results of R2R-CE and RxR-CE in Habitat simulator, R2R Unseen columns

results: GC-VLN achieves SR 33.6 on R2R-CE val-unseen, 2-3 points above the best training-free baseline InstructNav (31.0 SR), though its SPL (16.3) is below InstructNav's 24.0. On RxR-CE it reaches SR 33.8, beating all reported zero-shot methods (CA-Nav 19.0) and the supervised NaVid (23.8). Real-robot demos are qualitative only.
limitations: SPL is low (16.3 on R2R-CE, 13.8 on RxR-CE) because the exploration and backtracking paths are inefficient.
Depends on LLM decomposition and open-vocabulary object detection; failures include missed objects and misparsed spatial relations (e.g. 'through the door to the right' read as 'forward').
Real-world evaluation is only qualitative, and the constraint library uses hand-set default tolerances.
